Record-Breaking Airbus A350 Flight Lasted 24+ Hours, Crew Witnessed Two Sunsets and Two Sunrises
7 photos
Photo: Qantas
There are long flights, and then there are the flights going from Singapore to Newark, Bangalore to San Francisco, or Dubai to Auckland. These routes, operated by the likes of Singapore Airlines, Air India, or Emirates, usually take around 19 hours, and they put a lot of strain on passengers and crews alike. Imagine, then, how it will be like to fly for close to a full day, without landing.
That's what the flag carrier of Australia, Qantas , is planning, as it seeks to directly link, for the first time, Sydney to London and Sydney to New York. That's a distance of around 11,500 miles (18,500 km), which would take some 22 hours to complete.
As you're reading this, there is no operational plane capable of doing that. But there soon will be, and now there is an official Guinness World Record for the longest flight by distance by a commercial airliner to prove it.
The plane is called Airbus A350-1000ULR (Ultra-Long Range), and it is being specifically developed by the European aerospace giant to serve this particular Qantas requirement. It first flew in the summer of this year, and now it has officially broken the record mentioned above. Ok, maybe not right now, but we're only now learning about it, after its achievement was validated by the International Aeronautical Federation and Flightradar24.
Photo: Airbus Wearing callsign AIB35LR, the Airbus -operated flight took off from Melbourne, Australia at 17:27 local time (06:27 UTC) on Monday, 27 July and landed in Toulouse, France at 09:51 am local time (07:51 UTC) on Tuesday, 28 July.
It was not a direct, straight-line flight, but one that saw the plane fly over Sydney, head out over the Pacific towards Los Angeles, cross the North American continent, fly over the Atlantic Ocean and then the UK, and finally reach Toulouse. That's a total distance of 14,388 miles (23,155 km) over three continents and two oceans, which were covered in 24 hours and 24 minutes.
Because of the particularities of the flight (it flew east across 17 time zones and crossed the international date line), the crew on board, which counted a total of 13 people (three Airbus pilots, two Qantas pilots, seven Airbus engineers, and an International Aeronautical Federation rep), witnessed two sunrises and an equal number of sunsets. And that's something that doesn't happen very often on airplanes.
Photo: Airbus The record-setting flight is part of the test campaign for the A350-1000ULR, and the result of a specific request from Qantas to prove the plane can stay in the air this long, in a bid to simulate the very longest commercial operations possible.
But how did this plane manage to travel so far without landing or refueling? Well, Airbus did some modifications to the already very capable A350 base aircraft, the most important of which being the fitting of an additional rear center tank capable of carrying enough fuel to guarantee an extra 1,100 miles (1,800 km) of extra flight distance.
The plane was supposed to become operational in the Qantas fleet back in 2025, as per the provisions of the Australian airline's Project Sunrise , which is the official name of its quest to get its hands on the longest-range commercial airliner in the world.
Now, Airbus says it should be ready to fly commercially sometime in 2027, with the first route already decided upon: it will link Sydney to London. In the years to come, 11 more A350-1000ULR airplanes will join the Qantas fleet.
Photo: Airbus Normally, an A350-1000 can carry as many as 410 passengers at a time, but the 1000ULR will only transport 238, meaning the lowest seat density of any A350-1000 in service in the world. That is owed in part to the seating design chosen by the Australian airline.
Qantas opted back in 2023 to fit its dozen 1000ULRs with a brand-new, never-before-used Safran-made seating option called Unity. In words that are simple to understand, we're not dealing with seats per se, as you normally get in an aircraft, but miniature studios with their own doors, reclining seats, storage spaces, a hidden wardrobe, and even a 6.6-foot (two meters) bed to go with the 32-inch touchscreen with Bluetooth connectivity.
Each plane in the fleet will be fitted with 58 of these studios, of which only six will be available in first class, with all the fittings mentioned above. The rest will be deployed in business class in a somewhat scaled-down version, with a seat, storage spaces, a mirror, and a smaller, 18-inch screen. These studios don't come with a bed, but the seats can turn into that when the time comes.
When the 1000ULR goes operational next year, it will become the fourth passenger variant in the A350 family, joining the existing A350-900, A350-900ULR and the A350-1000. A fifth version, this time meant for cargo transport and called A350F, has just begun its flight test program. So far, says Airbus, there are 1,628 orders for the various A350 planes from 70 customers – of that, 740 are already flying in the service of 42 operators.

Beam Therapeutics’ risto-cel provided at least 12 consecutive months of freedom from severe pain crises for patients with sickle cell disease in a mid-stage trial, setting the stage for an FDA application as early as this year.
Beam Therapeutics’ cell therapy risto-cel freed patients with sickle cell disease from severe pain crises for at least one year, teeing up what could be the first application for a base-editing therapy, possibly by the end of this year.
“Positive pivotal results strengthen the risto-cel regulatory case and mark an important milestone for base editing,” H.C. Wainwright said in a Tuesday morning investor note.
Ristoglogene autogetemcel—dubbed risto-cel—met the Phase 1/2 BEACON trial ’s primary endpoint, Beam said on Tuesday, providing patients with sickle cell disease (SCD) with at least 12 consecutive months of freedom from severe vaso-occlusive crises (VOC)—or episodes of intense pain related to blocked vessels— based on independently adjudicated results. VOCs are a hallmark of SCD. As of Oct. 20, 39 adults and 10 adolescents had been treated with risto-cel, with 31 having completed the required follow-up period for the endpoint.
BEACON also succeeded on all secondary endpoints, which included freedom from hospitalization for severe VOCs for at least 12 consecutive months.
Risto-cel also met all of the trial’s primary safety endpoints at the interim analysis. The therapy’s profile was consistent with previously reported data from BEACON and with the known effects of the stem cell transplantation process.
In November 2024, Beam disclosed the death of a patient in BEACON, which according to the biotech occurred due to respiratory failure four months after receiving treatment. It was deemed unrelated to risto-cel and was instead “likely” linked to the busulfan-based chemotherapy immunosuppression regimen used in the stem cell transplant process.
The new Phase 1/2 readout will support an upcoming biologics license application (BLA), according to Beam. “With these results in hand, we are focused on submitting our planned BLA as early as year-end, which has the potential to be the first BLA for a base editing therapy,” Beam CEO John Evans said in a prepared statement.
While the FDA has approved gene-edited therapies from CRISPR Therapeutics and Genetix Biotherapeutics, Beam will likely be the first to seek marketing approval for a therapy that uses base editing. Also working on base editing is Eli Lilly, after the acquisition of Verve Therapeutics for up to $1.3 billion in 2025.

The biotech plans to present detailed results from BEACON at a medical meeting in 2027. BEAM will also present data from an earlier cutoff date at the American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans next month.
H.C. Wainwright noted that Beam did not disclose safety details nor the proportion of patients who achieved the primary efficacy endpoint.
“The topline data establishes endpoint success, while detailed safety, response rates and longer-term outcomes remain the next focus,” the firm said.
Risto-cel , formerly known as BEAM-101, is an ex vivo, autologous therapy comprising autologous CD34+ hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) that have been base edited. SCD happens when a mutation in the beta-globin gene causes a mutated form of adult hemoglobin to collect into long, rigid molecules that bend red blood cells into a sickle shape, according to Beam. The edit in risto-cel is meant to inhibit the BCL11A gene from blocking expression of fetal hemoglobin, thereby increasing production of the non-sickling and anti-sickling version of the protein.
At ASH, H.C. Wainwright will be looking for fetal hemoglobin (HbF) induction of over 60% and reduction of sickle hemoglobin to lower than 40%—"a ‘60/40’ trait that is viewed by physicians and regulators as a key goal in the treatment of SCD.”
Last month, analysts named Beam as one potential beneficiary of the FDA’s new plug-and-play guidance, under which gene-editing therapies addressing various disease-causing mutations could be covered under one BLA.
The new draft guidance “converts the individualized ‘product variant’ concept into an operational licensing framework, with base editing the template modality,” H.C. Wainwright said in a note to investors late last month. The analysts specifically pointed to BEAM-304, currently in a Phase 1/2 trial for phenylketonuria (PKU). BEAM-304 is designed to correct mutations in the phenylalanine hydroxylase gene that cause the disease. In North America and Europe, there are thought to be four specific mutations that cause PKU.

ACT Expo opened registrations for next year’s show with an agenda that leads with cutting fleets’ fuel and operating costs, starting with diesel technology. ACT Expo will take place May 17-20 at the Las Vegas Convention Center.
The cost-first pitch is new for a show whose 2026 event saw Rivian and Mack Trucks leaders on the keynote stage under a banner of digital and clean fleet technology. ACT Expo’s release places diesel prices “at the top of fleet concerns.” Fleets heading to Las Vegas in May will find the program opening on fuel efficiency.
The backdrop of record high fuel prices is behind the programming shift. U.S. on-highway diesel averaged a record $6.529 a gallon the week of Sept. 21, according to the Energy Information Administration’s weekly Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update . It was the latest in a string of all-time highs in September. The average was $6.127 the week of Nov. 9 according to the EIA.
“This isn’t just a sustainability conversation anymore; it’s a business imperative,” Erik Neandross, founder of ACT Expo, said in the release.
How the 2027 agenda differs from 2026
The updated agenda reflects a changing fleet landscape. ACT Expo announced its 2026 agenda in November 2025. That release said the program built on the show’s “long-standing leadership in clean transportation” while adding AI, autonomy, connectivity and software-defined vehicles. Diesel appeared in one listed session, on diesel and hybrid efficiency, and the release did not mention fuel prices.
The 2027 release opens its program list with reducing fuel and operating costs through diesel technology, aerodynamics, right-sizing, telematics and AI-enabled fleet management. Electric, hybrid, hydrogen and natural gas stay on the program, grouped under matching “the right technologies for the right applications.” EV infrastructure, including megawatt charging, keeps its own spot on the list.
The change is also being noted in the makeup of vehicles that will be present at the event. Last year’s announcement promised more than 200 “low- and zero-emission vehicles” on display. For 2027, the count is more than 200 “advanced commercial vehicles.”
Natural gas trucks were a heavy presence at the show from 2011 through 2018 before its focus shifted toward electric trucks, FreightWaves reported in a 2023 look at how ACT Expo grew into trucking’s “big splash.” Those trucks still had a place on the 2026 floor, where Westport showed its next-generation CNG fuel system on a Volvo VNL . ACT Expo notes natural gas will again be one of the key technologies in 2027.
Registration offers and expo hall
Early bird rates run through Dec. 11. ACT Expo added two registration offers for fleets and shippers. A team package adds complimentary passes for qualifying team members when a company buys two, and qualifying first-time fleet and shipper attendees may be eligible for a free pass.
Continuing education credit returns for a second year. In 2026, more than 25 sessions and 10 workshops were approved for credit through NAFA Fleet Management Association and Green Business Certification Inc.
The exhibit hall opens May 18-19. Presenting sponsors are Daimler Truck North America, Penske Transportation Solutions and Geotab. WSP produces the show.
ACT Expo’s Fleet Planning Committee, whose members collectively manage hundreds of thousands of commercial vehicles, shaped an agenda built around the investment decisions that matter most to fleets, according to the release.
“Every investment decision matters, and understanding which technologies can deliver real savings and operational improvements has never been more critical,” Neandross said.
Why it matters: Fleet buyers setting 2027 equipment budgets can weigh diesel efficiency upgrades against electric, natural gas and hydrogen trucks on one show floor in May. While the conference themes have changed, the focus on fleet efficiency regardless of powertrain remains.

By: Northern Miner Staff November 10, 2026
Scorpio Gold (TSXV, Nasdaq: SGLD) has hit high-grade gold 850 metres from the core resource area at its Manhattan project in Nevada, opening a new target for drilling beyond the ground that has anchored its exploration program. Drill hole 26MN-133 at April Fool cut 13.05 metres at 9.4 grams gold per tonne from 78.63 metres depth, the company said Tuesday . It is the target’s first deep diamond drill hole in a systematic program. “That opens the potential to extend the mineralized system well beyond the current resource footprint,” CEO Zayn Kalyan said in the statement. The result gives Scorpio a target beyond Manhattan’s existing gold inventory. Further holes must establish its size and continuity: the latest intersection doesn’t demonstrate continuous mineralization across the 850-metre gap, and its true width remains unknown.
Historical ground
Manhattan covers about 4,780 hectares in Nevada’s Walker Lane mineral belt, 53 km north-northeast of Tonopah and roughly four hours by road from Las Vegas. Scorpio owns the district outright, including Goldwedge and four former open pits acquired from Kinross Gold (TSX: K; NYSE: KGC) in 2021. The June 2025 resource covering Goldwedge and the Manhattan pit areas holds 18.34 million inferred tonnes at 1.26 grams gold, containing 740,000 ounces. Historical estimates covering April Fool and other satellite areas are excluded from that current resource. Earlier exploration at April Fool included reverse-circulation drilling used for a 1997 estimate, but detailed drill logs, collar coordinates and assay records have not survived, Scorpio said. The target is historical exploration ground now being tested with new core drilling. Scorpio’s broader program targets at least 50,000 metres of drilling across Manhattan. The district’s past-producing operations, historical drilling database and existing water rights provide a starting point for testing extensions and additional targets. Scorpio’s American depositary shares rose 0.8% stronger to $3.38 (C$4.73) Tuesday morning on Nasdaq, valuing the company at about $58 million. They’ve traded between $3.21 and $14.15 in the past year.

By: Northern Miner Staff November 10, 2026
U.S. government lenders aren’t planning to approve $1.6 billion (C$2.26 billion) in financing for a Kazakh tungsten venture linked to President Donald Trump’s sons, amid concerns about its commercial prospects and geopolitical risks, Bloomberg reported Monday. The U.S. Export-Import Bank and International Development Finance Corp. issued letters of interest last year for the Cove Kaz Capital Group project. Officials are concerned about its viability and Kazakhstan’s position between China and Russia, Bloomberg said, citing people familiar with the matter. Cove Kaz executive chairman Pini Althaus told the news agency that the company had received no indication of withdrawn support and didn’t expect to apply formally for loans until a feasibility study is completed next year. A Development Finance Corp. official said the agency wasn’t currently pursuing a transaction with the company.
Planned refinery
The uncertainty tests Washington’s efforts to develop tungsten supply outside China. The financing envisaged up to $900 million from the export bank and $700 million from the development lender, but the letters were expressions of interest rather than approved loans. Cove Kaz owns 70% of the venture developing Northern Katpar and Upper Kairakty, about 25 km apart in Kazakhstan , with national mining company Tau-Ken Samruk holding the rest. The company expects to finish the Northern Katpar feasibility study before the end of 2027 and plans a refinery in Kazakhstan to produce ammonium paratungstate, an intermediate tungsten product. Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr.’s investment connection runs through Skyline Builders Group (Nasdaq: KAZR). Cove Kaz and Skyline abandoned their merger on Nov. 2. Cove Kaz instead plans a direct U.S. listing in the first half of 2027 and announced a conditional $32-million equity commitment from American Ventures, implying a $1.97-billion valuation.

Simtra BioPharma Solutions has opened Building H, a more than $250 million expansion at its Bloomington, Ind., campus that gives the company more room to make sterile injectable drugs.
What’s Related
The contract manufacturer held a ribbon-cutting on Monday for the 153,000-square-foot building. Indiana Gov. Mike Braun, Bloomington Mayor Kerry Thomson, and other local officials joined company leaders. Construction started in June 2024.
Building H adds prefilled syringe filling, vial filling, and lyophilization, the freeze-drying step many injectable drugs need to stay stable. WFIU reported that the building was designed for high-speed isolator syringe filling lines and several large freeze dryers.
“Building H represents much more than additional manufacturing capacity. It is an important milestone in the growth strategy we are executing across Simtra,” said Franco Negron, Simtra’s chief executive officer. “We are investing in the capacity, technology and infrastructure our customers need to develop and manufacture increasingly complex sterile injectable medicines.”
Part of a bigger build-out
Building H is one piece of a larger plan. Simtra has also invested more than $125 million in added space at its Halle, Germany, site and an initial $150 million-plus in its new Bloomington Park Campus. All told, the company plans to grow from 11 filling lines to 18 by 2027 across its U.S. and European network.
“Our customers are planning years ahead, and they need manufacturing partners that can do the same,” said Ray Guidotti, chief operating officer. “Building H gives us significant new capacity in Bloomington today to go along with our expansion in Halle, while investment in our new Park campus creates additional options for the future. Together, these investments give customers greater flexibility in where and how they manufacture and provide a foundation that can scale as their programs grow.”
For drugmakers , that means more choice about where to place a product and more room to ramp up as a drug moves from clinical trials to commercial volumes.
A boost for Bloomington
Simtra says the expansion is expected to create “hundreds of high-quality jobs ” in Bloomington. WFIU reported that the company has created 450 jobs so far.
“You’re looking at 250 million dollars, hundreds of jobs and you’re investing a quarter of a billion,” Braun said at the event, according to WFIU. “That says a lot, so you’re lucky to be the community that’s getting the benefit of it.”
Thomson pointed to the reach of what gets made there. “People who live and work in Bloomington are helping produce therapies that can make an enormous difference in the lives of people they will never meet,” she said.
“Opening Building H is an important achievement for our Bloomington team and for everyone who has helped bring this expansion from concept to reality,” said Pat Adams, vice president of expansion operations. “It also creates a strong foundation for the continued growth of our Bloomington operations.”

Posted By: Mining.com Staff November 10, 2026
Meridian Mining (TSX: MNO; LSE: MNO) is weighing indicative financing packages of $400 million (C$565 million) as it begins pre-construction work at its Cabaçal copper-gold project in Brazil’s Mato Grosso state.
The company received more than 20 proposals, including several offering more than $300 million in debt. Several $400-million packages cover project debt, cost overruns, any required equity contribution, and offtake and marketing services, Meridian said Monday.
“To build Cabaçal, we need to arrange project finance, and this has been in planning since 2024,” CEO Gilbert Clark said. “I am not surprised by the strength of the project finance indicative proposals received from the various financial, trading, and industrial groups involved in the process.”
Cabaçal’s September feasibility study put initial capital costs at $322 million. Meridian, which reported a treasury of about $90 million, is shortlisting preferred financing bidders for detailed negotiations before a final investment decision.
Early works
Meridian has committed to $30.9 million in pre-construction contracts, including an engineering, procurement and construction management agreement with AFRY. Other commitments cover power transformers, bridge and road upgrades, a semi-autogenous grinding mill, Jameson flotation cells and an IsaMill for fine grinding.
Cabaçal lies about 320 km west-northwest of Mato Grosso’s capital, Cuiabá. Meridian has secured an installation licence and a declaration of public utility for a planned 24.3-km, 138-kilovolt power line linking the site to the Araputanga substation and Brazil’s national grid.

JLR takes BYD to court over its Defender-like SUV
After BYD opened orders for the Ti 7 in Europe and the UK in late July, many ( including us at Electrek ) compared it to the iconic Land Rover Defender, with its boxy, rugged (yet still elegant) SUV design.
BYD even described it as having “an unapologetically boxy profile” that delivers “the imposing, chunky design that finds favour among SUV buyers, yet delivers a contemporary look.”
Apparently, JLR has also taken notice. According to a report from The Times , court bailiffs acting on behalf of the British luxury automaker raided BYD’s offices in the Netherlands and seized digital records.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The raid comes ahead of a preliminary court ruling on Wednesday, which will determine whether BYD’s Ti7 SUV infringes on the intellectual property of the Land Rover Defender.
JLR believes BYD stripped down the Defender to reverse engineer some of its technology. Before the raid, BYD claims it fully cooperated with JLR’s requests.
BYD Ti 7 (Source: BYD)
According to local reports, BYD’s lawyers called JLR’s raid a “fishing expedition” and claimed, “too many files were seized.”
JLR declined to comment, while BYD said it had no comment at this time as it’s in an ongoing legal case.
The Ti 7 is on sale starting at £47,995 ($64,000) in the UK, on the road. That’s over £20,000 ($26,500) less than the plug-in Defender 110, which starts at £71,840 ($95,500) in the UK.
It has a seven-seat arrangement, which BYD said was specifically designed for the European and UK markets.
As the first vehicle in the UK based on its DM-p (Dual Mode performance) powertrain, BYD said the Ti 7 “vastly exceeds the closest competition,” seemingly another jab at the Defender.
The setup uses three electric motors and a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine, delivering a combined 402 hp (408 PS), enabling it to accelerate from 0 to 62 mph in 4.8 seconds.
BYD Ti 7 (Source: BYD)
The engine primarily powers a 35.6 kWh BYD Blade Battery, which provides a pure-electric WLTP driving range of up to 74 miles. In the city, it has an electric range of up to 102 miles.
Available exclusively in the UK in the flagship Excellence AWD trim, BYD claims that the Ti 7 offers “a level of equipment that exceeds anything that its rivals can offer at this price point.”
With the preliminary ruling scheduled for Wednesday, we should learn more about the BYD and JLR legal battle soon. Check back for updates as this is an ongoing story.

AMD EPYC 9686F-Top 1
At long last, the day is here. Today, we finally get to share with you our first look at AMD’s EPYC “Venice” series, or the EPYC 9006 processors.
Following AMD’s biennial CPU development roadmap, the highlight of the year for AMD’s CPU teams is the launch of the EPYC 9006 processors and the Zen 6 CPU architecture that underlies them. Admidst an unprecidented explosing in demand for server CPUs for AI systems to drive both host nodes and agnetic workloads, AMD finds itself in a very commanding position, bringing to market a new generation of even more powerful server hardware right when the industry seems to need it most. All the while, AMD has ambitions of becoming the undisputed market leader for server CPUs – ambitions that Venice seems primed to help AMD reach.
As far as server CPU launches go, today’s launch is remarkable on multiple levels. Besides taking a look at a wholly new server platform from AMD (socket and all), which would normally be a big event in and of itself, the server boom has turned the CPU development cycle on its head, and now it is a server CPU where we will see AMD’s latest CPU architecture. So along with our first benchmarks of Venice, today also marks our first chance to evaluate the Zen 6 CPU architecture that will be driving so many AMD products over the coming two years – everything ranging from server chips like Venice and Verano to consumer desktops, laptops, and more. There is a lot to unpack with today’s launch.
AMD EPYC: Generation on Generation
 | EPYC 9004 | EPYC 9005 | EPYC 9006 (SP7)
Codename | Genoa | Turin | Venice
Microarchitecture | Zen 4 | Zen 5 | Zen 6
Core Manufacturing | 5nm | 4nm/3nm | 2nm
Max Cores/Threads | 128/256 | 192/384 | 256/512
Core Complex | 16 + 32MB | 16 + 32MB | 32 + 128MB
Memory Support | 12x DDR5-4800 | 12x DDR5-6400 | 16x DDR5-8000 / MRDIMM-12800
Memory Capacity | 6TB | 6TB | 8TB
PCIe (1P) | 5.0 x128 | 5.0 x128 | 6.0 x96
Socket | SP5 | SP5 | SP7
Peak Power | 400W | 500W | 600W
With so much to do and so little time to do it all, we are going to have a lot more content to follow. But to get things started, for today’s launch piece we are going to run the flagship EPYC 9996 through not only our agentic-workload focused AgentSTH V7 benchmark suite, but we are also including bits and pieces of what is essentially a preview of 2027’s AgentSTH V8. For some context, we are going back roughly a decade in server architectures to not just blindly pick up benchmark suites, but to profile workloads on dozens of platforms for inclusion in the suite.
EPYC 9006 Die Shots (SP7 Zen 6c, ZP7 Zen6, SP8 Zen 6c, SP8 Zen 6)
We have lots of numbers for this one and some neat comparison points. The headline feature is that we now get up to 256 cores per socket, a new PCIe Gen6 I/O subsystem, and more than twice the memory bandwidth to go along with a revised Zen 6 microarchitecture and SoC design. AMD is also splitting its lineup into multiple families for different applications with two primary sockets, a return of the -X high-cache parts with Venice-X, and the LPDDR5X Verano. The new series covers a lot more and is by far the most ambitious innovation in the EPYC line since the switch to an I/O die, which allowed the EPYC 7002 to deliver a knockout . This is the Knockout Part Deux.
Also, I just wanted to recognize Ryan, Sam, and Vic for contributing to a quick turnaround on this one. We will have Ryan cover the Zen 6 microarchitecture and SoC portion before I take back over on performance. Regular STH readers may have noticed this, but many of our pieces are much longer than they used to be, and doing these reviews has become a team effort.
AMD EPYC 9006 “Venice”: The Story So Far
Over the summer, AMD held a proper unveiling for its EPYC 9006 “Venice” server CPU platform at the company’s annual Advancing AI event. In what has become AMD’s marquee event of the year – and a reflection of the importance of server parts to their bottom line – the company laid out an aggressive plan for 2026 and beyond. Spearheaded by the Venice CPU platform, AMD has ambitions to deliver not only their most powerful and most capable server platform to date, but to iterate on that over the next year or so to deliver a broad portfolio of server chips that covers everything from rank-and-file servers to mighty HPC systems, and of course lots of AI nodes.
AMD Venice Launch Deck- Six Generations of EPYC
Now in its sixth generation of Zen-architecture server chips, Venice is in some respects AMD’s most aggressive design yet. AMD is making heavier use of chiplets than ever before, and the company is now relying on advanced packaging techniques to tie them all together. This has allowed AMD to fully leverage TSMC’s N2 (2nm) process node, their first GAAFET-based node, to the best of their abilities, tapping it to not only devote more transistors than ever to the Zen CPU cores to boost their performance, but to pack in more CPU cores than ever before.
AMD Venice Launch Deck – Venice Improvements over Turin
For high-throughput workloads, the highlight of Venice is that there are now up to 256 CPU cores in a single socket, a 33% improvement over EPYC 9005 “Turin” only a generation ago – and with 20% higher IPC and higher clockspeeds on top of that. Meanwhile for workloads where single-threaded performance and latency are more critical, AMD is bringing the 5.3GHz EPYC 9686F to market to double-down on Zen 6’s IPC improvements with the highest clockspeeds yet for an EPYC server chip.
AMD is keen to tap into the agentic era of computing. And there are a lot of improvements to Venice and the Zen 6 CPU architecture that are going to help them get there. But do not underestimate the chip in other areas, either; AMD has invested in features such as PCIe Gen6, new virtualization and security features, and it has even picked up a software engineering firm in recent months to develop software to replace DRAM with flash memory. AI is certainly the highlight of the Venice story, but it is not the only story.
AMD Venice Launch Deck – AMD Server CPU Revenue Share
With any luck, AMD expects that over the next 12 months they will finally reach the point where they capture leadership of the server CPU market. As we saw with AMD’s earnings last week , the company’s data center division is already projecting that its revenues will surpass Intel’s in Q4 of this year. Meanwhile, AMD is already at 46% of the revenue share for the x86 server CPU market, and the company seems confident that Venice will help push them above 50% for the very first time.
EPYC 9006 SP7 Product Stack: Venice HF Gets a Spec Bump
Alongside its initial summer announcement of the EPYC 9006 lineup, AMD also published the complete specifications for its full stack of chip SKUs. This was for both the high-end SP7 platform launching today, as well as the more restrained SP8 platform that is launching early next year.
As it turns out, AMD was sandbagging things a bit. Whereas their flagship high-frequency chip, the EPYC 9686F, was originally announced to ship with a peak frequency of 5.0GHz, that is no longer the case.
AMD EPYC 9686F Clockspeed Upgrade
Instead, the 9686F is now a 5.3GHz chip. Making this a notable improvement just ahead of the launch of the hardware, and admittedly a bit of a point of pride (or at least bragging rights) for AMD.
In talking with AMD, the company has found that the final silicon for their big Zen 6 CCD has turned out even better than the company was expecting. Consequently, their earlier SKU stack was a bit conservative, and they can do a bit better than 5.0GHz – and allow the fastest Venice to clock higher than the fastest Turin after all.
So here is what the final, shipping SP7 chip stack looks like.
AMD EPYC 9006 SP7 SKUs
 | CPU Cores | Threads | Max Boost Clock | Base Clock | L3 Cache | TDP
AMD EPYC 9996 | 256 | 512 | 4.1 GHz | 2.55 GHz | 1024 MB | 600W
AMD EPYC 9966 | 192 | 384 | 4.0 GHz | 2.9 GHz | 768 MB | 600W
AMD EPYC 9846 | 168 | 336 | 3.7 GHz | 2.85 GHz | 768 MB | 500W
AMD EPYC 9756 | 128 | 256 | 4.0 GHz | 3.15 GHz | 512 MB | 500W
AMD EPYC 9G76 | 96 | 192 | 4.8 GHz | 3.4 GHz | 384 MB | 500W
AMD EPYC 9656 | 96 | 192 | 3.7 GHz | 3.05 GHz | 512 MB | 400W
AMD EPYC 9686F | 96 | 192 | 5.3 GHz | 3.4 GHz | 384 MB | 500W
AMD EPYC 9556 | 64 | 128 | 4.3 GHz | 2.75 GHz | 384 MB | 300W
AMD EPYC 9586F | 64 | 128 | 5.0 GHz | 3.75 GHz | 384 MB | 500W
Only the EPYC 9686F is getting a specification bump here. The rest of the lineup is unchanged from before. Notably, this means the 64 core EPYC 9586F does not get to share in the gains. So if customers want AMD’s highest clocked Venice chip, they will need to buy the 96 core version.

source_document.body:
Sportswear company ASICS is recovering misplaced products nearly 60% faster at its Byhalia, Mississippi, distribution center since it began conducting nightly flights of high-risk storage areas with autonomous inventory drones.
The drones, manufactured by Corvus Robotics, have increased counting frequency six-fold compared to the normal practice of counting inventory twice a year. The data collected each night is aggregated and now analyzed on a monthly basis, allowing orders to ship on time and at full price. The new system has saved about 200 hours of monthly counting labor, which ASICS has redirected into inventory research and exception management, the companies said Tuesday.
The ASICS facility holds close to 3 million items — 2.3 million pairs of footwear and 700,000 pieces of apparel and accessories — across roughly 44,000 stock keeping units, all managed in a Manhattan Associates warehouse management system. It fills e-commerce orders and ships to wholesale accounts, along with ASICS full price and outlet retail stores.
Corvus drones provide surveillance in the areas that tend to produce the most discrepancies — the singles area, where returned and single pair products get stored and picked, and case reserve. Both were counted twice a year under ASICS cycle count policy.
In one three-month stretch the drones surfaced 26 misplaced cases holding more than 200 pairs of shoes, products that would otherwise have stayed unavailable to customers until the next scheduled physical count.
“If a unit went missing, we might not find it for six months,” said Kyle Koestler, senior director of distribution and transportation at ASICS America Corp., in a news release. “That could be the last pair in the building for an order we’ve already taken, and then the customer gets a cancellation. With Corvus One, we’re cycle counting on a monthly basis so we can surface any errors sooner and ensure customer orders are delivered on time.”
The inventory control team is putting the 200 hours in time savings towards inventory reconciliation in the packing operation, root cause research and special projects for the wholesale business.
In both areas the drone does two jobs on the same pass, reading every Universal Product Code and counting the boxes in each location. In the singles area, returns mean the same SKU can show up several times in one location, so a UPC read on its own can get attached to the wrong box. Counting the boxes gives ASICS a physical total to check the scans against. If the drone counts 10 boxes, it should come back with 10 UPC reads, according to Corvus.
ASICS schedules seven flights a night, starting around 7 p.m. The aisles the drones fly in are less than six feet wide. The Corvus One drone flies using onboard computer vision and spatial reasoning, with no additional infrastructure anywhere in the building. Each morning an inventory associate reviews each flight and resolves most discrepancies from a desk, working off the video and images the drones capture of every location.
The accuracy provides a revenue benefit too. ASICS publishes availability feeds to online marketplaces. Before inventory management by drone the team held back 12 to 15 units out of every 100 to make sure it could deliver on what it promised. Product at the bottom of the lot never shows up on the marketplace, leaving ASICS having to liquidate the goods at a steep discount. ASICS now publishes the full feed and sells that product at full price, according to the announcement.
ASICS says using drones to count inventory also saves energy because employees are operating lift equipment through the aisles less frequently.
Corvus is based in Mountain View, California. Its customers include Southern Glazer’s Wine & Spirits, GNC, Dermalogica, and MSI Surfaces. Other companies offering warehouse inventory drones include Gather AI and Verity.

Lucid (LCID) says service wait times dropped 20% globally in the third quarter after it grew its technician and service-support staff by more than 40% in a single quarter.
The automaker is also adding Studio and Service Centers in Southern California, Los Angeles, Dallas, and the Chicago suburbs, plus 20 more Gravity Mobile Service vans. It’s a clear sign that service had become a problem for Lucid owners.
Lucid hires up service after a year of cuts
Lucid announced the numbers today, a day after its Q3 2026 earnings . Both comparisons are against the second quarter, not a year ago.
Lucid’s new combined Studio and Service Center in Mission Viejo, California (Image: Lucid)
The hiring isn’t done either. After a 40%-plus increase in technicians, advisors, and concierges in Q3, Lucid wants that figure at 50% by the end of 2026 and 60% by Q1 2027. Mobile Service capacity in North America grew 15%, with a 40% target for year-end.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
That’s a big hiring push for a company that laid off 18% of its workforce in June , its second cut in four months after a 12% reduction in February. Roughly 1,500 people left across those two rounds.
And owners noticed. On the LucidOwners forum, one Air Touring owner posted in early October that Lucid told them in writing to expect “a service time of about 7 weeks” at its Beverly Hills Service Center. Other threads blamed service-department layoffs for slow repairs and recall work.
A Lucid technician at work in a Service Center (Image: Lucid)
Billy Hayes, Lucid’s Chief Customer Officer, said the company is “adding service personnel, and increasing Mobile Service capacity to reduce wait times and provide more convenient, responsive support.”
The new Lucid service locations
Here’s what’s opening, according to Lucid:
Mission Viejo, California: a new combined Studio and Service Center, open now
Downtown Los Angeles and Dallas: Studio and Service Center operations later this year
Highland Park, Illinois: Q1 2027
Mobile Service: 20 additional Gravity Mobile Service vehicles in North America
Service bays at Lucid’s Mission Viejo location (Image: Lucid)
Lucid is also letting a growing number of its Certified Collision shops handle recall campaign work, which should take some pressure off its own Service Centers.
Outside the US, the expansion leans on partners. Munsterhuis Autobedrijven is Lucid’s first retail partner in the Netherlands (Hengelo), Cloppenburg Automobil SE opens a Duisburg retail and service site in January 2027, Autohaus Possögel starts authorized service in Naumburg, Germany, in December, and Emil Frey France will support Lucid’s launch in France. In Saudi Arabia, Lucid opened its first company-owned Body & Paint Repair Center in Riyadh, with more service sites in Riyadh and Dammam coming in the first half of 2027.
A Lucid Gravity converted for Mobile Service (Image: Lucid)
The numbers Lucid doesn’t give
Lucid doesn’t say what the average wait time actually is.
A 20% drop from seven weeks is still more than five weeks. A 20% drop from one week is a non-issue. Without a baseline, owners can’t tell which one they’re getting.
It’s also hard to separate better service from fewer cars coming in. Lucid delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3 , down 7% year-over-year, while it worked through inventory. Its fleet keeps growing, but slowly.
For context, Rivian delivered 19,248 vehicles in Q3, five times Lucid’s volume, and it’s been leaning hard on mobile service too. Lucid is a much smaller operation trying to cover the US, Europe, and the Middle East with a thin network.
Electrek’s Take
This is the right move, and it’s overdue.
Lucid has been one of the few EV startups with genuinely class-leading hardware. The Air’s efficiency is still unmatched and the Gravity is a great vehicle on paper, even if we found its software wasn’t ready . But when you’re asking someone to spend $80,000 or more on a car from a brand with an uncertain future, the ownership experience is half the sale. A seven-week wait for a repair kills that sale, and the referrals that come after it.
So growing service staff by 40% in a quarter is a big deal. It also tells you how thin those teams had gotten after two rounds of layoffs. Lucid cut too deep in the wrong place, and it’s now hiring to fix it.
The problem is the timing and the money. Lucid burned $1.04 billion in free cash flow in Q3 and only stays funded into late 2027 because the PIF just added another $1.75 billion. Meanwhile, the Midsize “Cosmos” that’s supposed to bring real volume doesn’t start production until the second half of 2027. Service is exactly where Lucid should spend between now and then, because the buyers it has today are the ones who’ll decide whether anybody trusts the brand with a cheaper EV.

Wing, the drone delivery business of Alphabet ( NASDAQ: GOOG ), said it will invest $125 million to build a 15,000-square foot manufacturing facility in Fort Worth, Texas, over the next two years to meet growing interest from retailers in ultra-fast delivery.
The company also plans to launch drone delivery in Japan, in partnership with KDDI Corp.
Upcoming U.S. rules of the road, expected at any moment, will serve as a trigger for widespread expansion, Wing said.
The new Texas facility will be able to produce tens of thousands of unmanned aerial aircraft each year, supporting Wing’s aggressive plan to expand drone delivery service nationwide as consumers increasingly opt for the convenience of home delivery for last-minute needs, Wing announced Friday. Some of the investment will also support r&d in California.
The news release is the first time Wing has given projections for its fleet size.
Wing, which operates from more than 70 sites, is working to expand to nearly 20 U.S. markets next year, making drone delivery available to more than 40 million people through its partnership with Walmart . Wing currently operates limited service in five metropolitan areas, including Central Florida, Houston, Atlanta and Dallas-Fort Worth. The partners say the drone delivery network will stretch across more than 270 store locations across the nation, including Los Angeles, Cincinnati, San Diego, Miami and Philadelphia.
Cruising at speeds up to 60 mph, Wing’s aircraft can carry up to five pounds of goods. Wing says it has made more than 1 million residential deliveries so far, usually within 30 minutes.
In September, Wing began a pilot delivery program for Lowe’s , enabled by the DoorDash marketplace. Fast-casual restaurant Panera is testing Wing delivery in North Carolina.
Walmart is not relying on a single drone delivery provider. Last week, it announced plans to create a nationwide delivery network operated by Zipline from 300 store locations. Zipline said it raised $1.5 billion to ramp up manufacturing of its aircraft.
Why It Matters: Drones are the latest front in the quick commerce wars, offering retailers and marketplaces another mode for satisfying consumer expectations for convenience and speed when ordering online. Orders prepared at fulfillment centers are typically delivered in one to five days by courier companies, while store-to-door fulfillment takes advantage of app-based delivery platforms and crowd-sourced drivers to make deliveries in one to three hours.
Regulatory Opening
The Federal Aviation Administration’s highly anticipated rulemaking on beyond-visual-line-of-sight is expected to unleash the next-generation of commercial drone activity as operators will be able to scale drone delivery and other applications more broadly. Under the current process, operators are required to operate drones within visual line of sight unless holding an individual waiver.
The final rule, under review by the White House since July, was delayed from its February publication because administration officials wanted to make sure it could accommodate future technology developments and didn’t favor large companies. Industry officials have chaffed at the lengthy rulemaking process, saying the lack of certainty about rules of the road is inhibiting investment.
As proposed, the BVLOS rule would allow drone operations to occur at or below 400 feet above ground level from pre-designated, secure-access locations. All operators will need FAA approval for the area where they intend to fly and indicate the approximate number of daily operations, as well as takeoff, landing and loading areas.
Drone operators will have to utilize Automated Data Service Providers to support large-scale BVLOS activity and ensure drones are safely separated from each other and manned aircraft. A BVLOS operator could be its own data service provider or contract with another company. Drones also would have technologies that enable them to automatically detect and avoid crewed aircraft broadcasting their position with ADS-B surveillance technology.
Large fleets like those of Wing would require an FAA operating certificate, with the agency conducting more oversight of ongoing operations and requiring operators to develop a safety management system and training program.
On Monday, the FAA issued the first of its kind authorization for a drone to fly beyond the operator’s visual line of sight from the U.S. coastline over the Gulf of Mexico. The authorization allows Skyways to operate its autonomous V2 vertical takeoff and landing aircraft from Shell’s SPLC facility in Gibson, Louisiana, to a Shell platform in the Gulf to inspect a pipeline right-of-way and simulate delivery of equipment to the platform.
In a sign that the drone space is becoming more attractive from an investment standpoint, Axon Enterprise Inc., a public safety and defense technology company best known for making Taser electroshock weapons, last week announced a $1.2 billion investment in Skydio, increasing its ownership stake in the drone company to 37%. Skydio sells drones for physical security, mapping, asset inspection and national security applications.
Japan
Wing is partnering with KDDI Corp. to bring its drone delivery service to select areas in Japan by the end of 2027. Demand for new delivery options is expected to be strong because of a declining working-age population and a declining delivery driver workforce.
Initial deployment will focus on food delivery. The companies will work with local governments and other partners to expand service to daily necessities, over-the-counter medications, and small retail items, according to an Oct. 26 news release.
Wing will provide autonomous drones, flight systems and automated ground infrastructure while KDDI, a telecommunications company, will provide the communication infrastructure, regulatory compliance and market development.
Zipline noise breakthrough
Meanwhile, Zipline has reengineered how its drones fly to reduce noise, a common complaint heard in neighborhoods, the company said last month. While most drones must continuously run all their motors in order to stay in the air, Zipline drones feature a fixed wing that allows them to fly like planes and turn off all but one motor once they reach cruising speed and altitude.
With dynamic flying, Zipline drones now transition to on-wing flight more efficiently while producing less noise, using wind and gravity to accelerate and decelerate, similar to birds taking advantage of air currents.
Instead of static, pre-planned trajectories, Zipline’s dynamic flying optimizes for reduced sound by balancing wind, altitude, and speed. As a Zipline drone takes off, it uses its weather sensors to measure the real-time wind conditions. It then combines that data with a custom sound model to determine the quietest way to transition to on-wing flight, such as dipping its nose to gain speed like a bike going downhill, or popping upwards to quietly slow down at the end of a flight.
Now deployed fleetwide, sound-optimized dynamic flying reduces flight times too, Zipline said. Flight times are 53 seconds shorter on average because of faster transitions in and out of on-wing flight.

The fully electric Whitby Morrison ice cream van, built on the Mercedes-Benz eSprinter, photographed in Crewe, England.
The “world’s leading ice cream truck manufacturer” has released its first fully electric ice cream truck, which is already in operaiton, and it says it’s open for orders for more.
Whitby Morrison bills itself as “the world’s leading ice cream truck manufacturer,” supplying converted vans as ice cream trucks to drivers worldwide.
And now it has taken a big step into the modern age delivering its first fully electric ice cream truck to Hocking’s dairy in North Devon, England.
The truck has been operating since July, through the course of one “ice cream season.” It reportedly covered more than 100 miles a day and has done days serving up to 12 hours at a time.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
It’s built on a standard Mercedes eSprinter, so it’s not retrofitted from the diesel vans that make up most of Whitby Morrison’s other offerings. The eSprinter comes in a “chassis cab” configuration which comes with just the chassis and cab, and lets upfitters build whatever they want onto the back end of the vehicle.
In this case, it also got some pretty extensive (and a little over-the-top) art all around the vehicle, highlighting the van’s electric operation.
(Battery-powered soft-serve machine needs no engine/generator running)
The ice cream truck maker, Whitby Morrison, says this is the “world’s first fully certified electric ice cream truck.”
We’re not sure what sort of international certifications are required for an ice cream truck so we’ll take their word for it, but we have seen a Rivian EDV turned into a Ben & Jerry’s ice cream truck , complete with side window, and a concept electric ice cream truck as far back as 2019 . So it’s certainly not the very first time this idea has been had, at least.
And it is a good idea. As with school buses , ice cream trucks are vehicles that children are likely to congregate around. Having a stinky old truck spewing emissions just a few feet away from those kids’ lungs is the sort of thing that can expose them to a life of health problems… and we might as well not stack that on top of the sugar addiction we’re teaching them to have (hey, at least they have to get outside to chase the truck down, so they’re getting some physical activity out of it, right?)
It also opens up more possibilities for operators to serve at events where having a diesel truck running might not be reasonable, like in enclosed spaces or where quiet might be appreciated (this came up when we went to Harbinger Motors’ factory opening , where local food trucks were in attendance, inside the large factory building, and made the air quality noticeably worse).
Whitby Morrison says it’s taking orders both in the UK and overseas, with US orders just opening. To learn more, head on over to its website .

350-HP 2027 Chevrolet Colorado EPA Gas Mileage Ratings Are Now Live
66 photos
Photo: Chevrolet / EPA / edited
GM has found a few additional horsepower for the 2027 model year Colorado, but somebody checking the Monroney sticker won't find much reason to celebrate. Per the Environmental Protection Agency's published ratings, the mid-size pickup generally returns the same combined gas mileage as the 2026 model. Only a few changes between city and highway driving are worth your attention.
The worst offender here is the ZR2 with the Bison package, which drops to a thirsty 15 miles per gallon combined. Instead of the previous L3B version of the 2.7-liter turbocharged inline-four engine, 2027 models feature the L4B. Maximum output climbs from 310 to 350 horsepower, while peak torque is now listed as 450 pound-feet (610 Newton-meters) instead of 430 lb-ft (583 Nm).
How did General Motors do it? First and foremost, the Detroit-based automaker switched to a different turbocharger. Redesigned pistons also need highlighting, and updated fuel injection hardware seals the deal. As ever, prospective customers are presented with an eight-speed automatic transmission and either rear- or four-wheel drive.
There are two distinct 4WD transfer cases to speak of. The lesser unit is a two-speed affair, whereas the heavy-duty transfer case of the ZR2 was designed specifically for off-road shenanigans. Base 4WD trucks get open rear diffs that rely on StabiliTrak brake-actuated traction control to manage wheel spin. Higher up the spectrum, there's the G80 auto-locking rear diff and the ZR2's electronic push-button locker. The ZR2 also features a full-locking front diff.
Having cleared that up, it's worth remembering how the EPA actually measures gas mileage. The agency uses a five-cycle testing framework, covering heavy urban traffic, highway driving, higher-speed and more aggressive acceleration, cold-weather operation with the cabin heater running, and driving the vehicle with the AC on to measure the extra powertrain and battery load.
Photo: Chevrolet With that out of the way, the Colorado 2WD provides the least complicated direct comparison between the 2027 and 2026 model years. Now good for 20 mpg city, 24 mpg highway, and 21 mpg combined, the Colorado 2WD used to achieve 19 mpg city, 24 mpg highway, and 21 mpg combined. The combined figure can be read as 11.2 liters per 100 kilometers in metric lingo.
The base Colorado 4WD gets 19 mpg (12.4 l/100 km) in the combined test cycle, with the new truck improving city mileage by 1 mpg while sacrificing 2 mpg on the highway. Upgrading to the ZR2 gets you 1 less mpg in the city while leaving highway and combined efficiency untouched from 2026.
The ZR2 with the Bison package, however, loses 2 mpg highway and 1 mpg combined from its 2026 model year equivalent. Make that 6.7 gallons of dinosaur brew per 100 miles, namely 15.7 liters per 100 kilometers, making it the least economical configuration in the EPA's 2027 model year listings. Only the ZR2 Bison suffered a decline in combined EPA gas mileage.
Even so, the additional torque is a great trade-off as long as the ZR2 Bison is used extensively off the beaten path. Additional torque also comes in handy when towing. Chevrolet quotes up to 7,700 pounds (3,493 kilograms) for model year 2027, while payload tops 1,710 pounds (776 kilograms). In this regard, nothing has changed from the 2026 model year Colorado midsizer.

A view of the Porcupine mine site. Credit: Discovery Mining via Facebook.
By: Northern Miner Staff November 10, 2026
Discovery Mining (TSX: DSV; US-OTC: DSVSF) reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings as lower depreciation helped offset rising gold costs at its Porcupine operations in Ontario. Adjusted earnings rose to $83 million (C$117 million), or 10¢ a share, from $61.1 million, or 8¢, a year earlier, Discovery said Tuesday . That beat the 7¢ consensus forecast expected by analysts. Production met expectations, but operating cash costs eere higher than expected, National Bank Financial mining analyst Rabi Nizami said Tuesday. “The beat on adjusted [earnings per share] and cash flow largely reflects lower depreciation and working capital movements,” Nizami said in a note. “Annual production and cost guidance was maintained, although cash costs are now expected at the top end of the range.” The results put the focus on Discovery’s ability to turn steadier milling into stronger returns as it revamps the Porcupine complex acquired last year. Updated resources and a technical report expected in early 2027 will help investors assess the operation’s growth plans, Nizami said.
Higher costs
Discovery produced a record 70,564 oz. gold in the quarter, 12% more than a year earlier. Operating cash costs rose 6% from the second quarter to $1,470 per oz., while all-in sustaining costs increased by the same percentage to $2,293 per oz., the company said Tuesday. Its full-year gold production target remains 260,000–300,000 oz., with operating cash costs expected at the top of the $1,250–$1,400 per oz. range. Output through September totalled 198,142 ounces. Free cash flow reached $86.9 million, helped by a $56.5-million working capital inflow, largely from the timing of payments to suppliers, Nizami said. Cash increased 24% from June to $450.7 million, leaving Discovery with liquidity to continue rebuilding Porcupine, he said.
Discovery is aiming to more than double Porcupine’s annual gold output to over 500,000 oz. by expanding existing mines and restarting Dome as a large open-pit deposit. The company is also evaluating a central gold processing facility at the recently acquired Kidd metallurgical site to handle ore from across the complex and support larger operations at Dome and Pamour.
Mining at Dome is expected to restart by early 2028, with first ore production in mid-2028.
Mexico spending
Discovery also said Tuesday it reduced this year’s spending forecast for its Cordero silver project in Mexico by $70 million to $20–30 million. That cut was expected because permit fees were lower than assumed, Nizami said. Mexico’s environmental department, SEMARNAT, approved the project through land-use and environmental impact permits announced last month. Discovery is updating construction and operating cost estimates from its 2024 feasibility study. Cordero lies about 200 km south of Chihuahua city. The 2024 study outlined a 19-year operation with initial construction costs of $606 million and average annual payable silver output of about 14 million oz. in the first decade, according to Discovery. Discovery shares dropped 4.4% to C$11.14 Tuesday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$9.1 billion (C6.5 billion)$. They have traded between C$5.47 and C$13.43 over the past year.

Coherus is narrowing its pipeline projects while Gyre reorganizes after an acquisition, with both biotechs conducting workforce reductions.
Coherus Oncology is shrinking its workforce by 30%, and Gyre Therapeutics is laying off an undisclosed number of workers after acquiring Cullgen.
For Coherus, the cuts stem from a reorganization that involves deprioritizing development of its investigational combination treatment in a range of cancers to focus on a lead indication of esophageal cancer. Last month, the biotech shared interim Phase 1b results for the cytolytic CCR8 antibody tagmokitug paired with toripalimab, with the duo demonstrating a confirmed overall response rate of 75% among patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in a front-line setting, irrespective of PD-L1 status.
Before the reorganization, Coherus had been studying the experimental duo across several indications, including head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, colorectal cancer and gastric cancer.
“The financial benefits of right-sizing the organization and reducing the scope of our forward-focused efforts provide substantial and durable benefits to our operating model,” Coherus CFO Bryan McMichael said in a Monday release. “These benefits will be realized over the next two quarters,” he said, adding that the efforts will lower the biotech’s quarterly core cash burn by $6 million.
The biotech did not reveal numbers behind the layoffs, but Coherus had 147 full-time and part-time employees as of Dec. 31, 2025. Based on that count, about 44 roles are likely impacted by the new cuts.
It’s the second time in less than two years that the California biotech has downsized by 30%. The last layoff wave occurred in March 2025 after Coherus’ divestment of Udenyca—a prescription drug used to reduce the chance of infection due to a low white blood cell count—to Intas Pharmaceuticals’ Accord BioPharma. The deal included a $483 million upfront payment to Coherus, money the biotech said it would use to repay $230 million in existing convertible notes due in 2026.

The company did not disclose the number of employees impacted from the Cullgen layoffs or its internal restructure and declined to provide BioSpace with additional comment.
In May, chronic disease–focused Gyre closed the all-stock buyout of Cullgen, a biotech focused on developing targeted protein degraders and degrader antibody conjugate therapies. Since then, Gyre has incorporated the biotech as a subsidiary. Before the acquisition, Cullgen employed over 120 staffers, according to a Gyre presentation filed with the SEC.

Stellantis Finally Sells Idled Brampton Plant, Canadian Defense Specialist Roshel Acquired It
7 photos
Photo: Stellantis
Stellantis has found a buyer for its Brampton vehicle assembly plant. While that may seem like good news, please do not confuse a return to manufacturing with a return to automotive production on the same scale. Canadian defense specialist Roshel wants to turn the former Chrysler factory into an advanced defense manufacturing center, potentially bringing hundreds of workers back.
Replacing a mass-production car factory with a defense contractor doesn't automatically restore historical production volumes, the previous headcount, or the supplier business that Brampton supported when it produced Dodge and Chrysler models there. Stellantis and Roshel have recently signed an asset purchase agreement covering the facility and its associated equipment.
Neither party has disclosed the purchase price, and the transaction does require government and regulatory approval. If everything goes according to plan, it should be completed by the end of 2026. Stellantis and Roshel are further exploring cooperation involving vehicle technologies and services tailored for the defense industry.
That being said, Brampton hasn't assembled a single road-going vehicle since December 2023. Its last hurrah included three familiar nameplates, beginning with the Chrysler 300 and mechanically similar Dodge Charger. The Challenger was also made there, for all three models featured mostly similar underpinnings and oily bits.
The final 300 rolled off the line on December 20 three years ago, whereas the last Charger and Challenger followed two days later. According to Dodge, the final units were a Destroyer Gray Scat Pack Widebody Charger and a Pitch Black SRT Demon 170 Challenger. The 300 had its own farewell earlier that month, with Chrysler bidding farewell to the full-size luxury sedan on December 8, 2023.
Photo: Stellantis That final car was a HEMI-powered 300C finished in Velvet Red. Following these models, Brampton was supposed to have another Stellantis automotive chapter in the form of the Jeep Compass. The multinational automaker suspended the program in February 2025, moving Compass production to Belvidere in Illinois.
Unfortunately, this change of plans resulted in a Brampton workforce that remained on extended layoff. The prospect of a new vehicle program gradually disappeared, affecting nearby automotive suppliers in the process. Now that Roshel is calling the shots, the Canadian defense company needs additional manufacturing space.
Chief executive officer Roman Shimonov made it clear that the company had outgrown its existing manufacturing and research facilities, with Shimonov also highlighting that Roshel had produced more than 2,500 vehicles for Ukraine alone. Meaningful business, for sure, and it's even more so for a relatively young company. More specifically, Roshel Defence Solutions was founded in Toronto a decade ago, back in 2016.
A passenger vehicle assembly plant, however, depends on sustained production volumes and large workforces. Defense manufacturers may also need complex supply chains and skilled workers, but their output revolves around government or institutional procurement contracts. Otherwise put, Roshel isn't going to operate anything resembling the production system of Stellantis at the Brampton plant.
Speaking of Stellantis, the defense specialist intends to lease a quarter of the property back to Stellantis for automotive work. What kind of work? According to The Globe and Mail, that would be "possible vehicle assembly." It's easy to imagine a military version of the Ram HD or the Jeep Gladiator, but so far, nothing has been confirmed by either Stellantis or Roshel in this regard.

Lotus Type 135 Will Be Powered by the Brand-New 671-HP Horse W40 Hybrid V8 Engine
9 photos
Photo: Horse Powertrain
As with most other projects in the automotive industry, British carmaker Lotus’ first supercar, the Type 135, is a bit behind schedule. Initially planned to be presented by the end of this year as a 2027 MY, the car is nowhere in sight. But now, at least, we know exactly what will power it.
News of that came not from Lotus, but from UK-based engineering firm Horse Powertrain . In the news a lot recently on account of the many different powertrains they developed, these guys now step into the spotlight as the makers of the engine that'll go into the Type 135.
The powerplant is called W40, and it is Horse's first V8 engine. And not just any V8 engine, but a hybrid-first contraption that promises huge amounts of power and, by extension, low fuel consumption.
As presented this week, the W40 is a 4.0-liter monster optimized for high-performance hybrid vehicles and rocking an advanced fuel injection system, shortened intake paths for the twin top-mounted turbochargers, and a brand-new transmission with eight speeds and a sportscar-grade wet dual clutch.
The power levels for the engine alone are satisfyingly high, with levels standing at 671 hp and 800 Nm of torque. The hybrid transmission, called 8LDCT, can withstand much more than that, though, up to 1,050 Nm of torque.
With these numbers, and factoring in the 441-pound (200 kg) weight of the hardware, the engine is described by Horse as one of the most power-dense V8 solutions available on the market at the time of writing.
It's not clear yet how those numbers transform into performance figures for the Type 135 , as that depends on a lot more factors, but we expect them to be on par with the raw figures mentioned above.
Horse hints the W40 hybrid engine will be deployed on a lot more vehicles, from sports cars to pickup trucks, as long as they're in need of a longitudinally mounted solution. On the list of targets for the powerplant are Horse's existing customers, carmakers Renault, Geely, Volvo, Proton, Nissan, and Mitsubishi.
As for the Type 35, the spiritual successor of the legendary Esprit, it will probably punch out more than what the W40 is capable of delivering, but we won't know more about that until closer to 2028, which is the year we now expect the vehicle to become available. Naturally, we will keep an eye on things and report back once we know more.
As for pricing, back in 2024, when the Type 135 was being considered as a purely electric car, the rumor mill talked about a sticker price that would read around 75,000 British pounds, which would be roughly $100,000 at today's exchange rates. It remains to be seen if that's still the case.
